title: Hacking of social media accounts - what the FIR should actually state
p1:
Your social media account was hacked. But will your FIR actually describe the crime clearly?

Many people write only: “My account was hacked.” That single sentence may not capture what really happened.
p2: A surprising fact: the details in the FIR can shape how the complaint is investigated. A vague complaint may miss important digital evidence that could identify the person behind the attack.
p3:
A useful FIR should mention specific facts: the platform involved, username or account details, when access was lost, suspicious login activity, unauthorized posts or messages, password changes, financial loss (if any), and any evidence like screenshots, emails, or alerts.

The key idea is simple: describe the digital actions, not just the feeling of being hacked. Clear facts create a clearer investigation path.
conclusion: If your account was compromised today, would you know what details to include in the FIR? What information do you think most people forget to mention?
